# Robot package format

A robot package is a folder that describes one robot to Kapto: its
`package.toml`, the robot's URDF and meshes, what it sends
(`streams.toml`, see [Configuration](../concepts/configuration.md)) and
which decoded value drives which joint (`mapping.toml`). Kapto finds the
packages in the folders of `paths.packages`; `kapto package list` shows
them and `kapto package show` one of them.

```toml
# What this package is. Kapto identifies a version of it by its ID and
# version, and by a hash of all its files (`kapto package show`).
id = "arm7"
version = "0.1.0"
name = "Sample seven-joint arm"
vendor = "Kapto"
description = "A generic seven-joint arm with a two-finger gripper, matching the synthetic robot in tools/kapto-loadgen."

# The robot description. What the robot sends and how it drives the joints
# are in streams.toml and mapping.toml, the default names.
urdf = "urdf/arm7.urdf"
```

## `package.toml`

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | The package's ID: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, e.g. `arm7`. Unique among the packages on one machine. |
| `version` | yes | The package's version as its author numbers them, e.g. `1.2.0`; text without spaces. With the content hash, it identifies a version of the package. |
| `name` | no | What people call the robot, e.g. `Sample seven-joint arm`. |
| `vendor` | no | Who makes the robot or wrote the package. |
| `description` | no | A sentence or two about the robot. |
| `contact` | no | Where to ask about the package, e.g. an email address or web page. |
| `urdf` | yes | The robot description, relative to the package folder, e.g. `urdf/arm7.urdf`. |
| `streams` | no | What the robot sends, relative to the package folder. `streams.toml` by default. |
| `mapping` | no | Which decoded value drives which joint, relative to the package folder. `mapping.toml` by default. |
| `layout` | no | How the live view and replays are arranged, relative to the package folder. `layout.toml` by default; without it, a layout is made from what the package declares. |

Paths are relative to the package folder and may not lead out of it.

## `qa.toml`

Which quality checks run on the episodes recorded with the package, and
their thresholds. Each check's settings are in the table named after its
ID; a check left out runs with its defaults, and so does every check of a
package without `qa.toml`. Every result records `qa_params_version`, so
results computed with different settings aren't taken for alike. Every
recording carries the `qa.toml` it was recorded with, and its episode
is checked with that copy, so editing the package later never changes
an episode's results.

```toml
# Which quality checks run on the episodes recorded with this package, and
# their thresholds. Each check's settings are in the table named after it;
# a check left out runs with its defaults. Change `qa_params_version`
# whenever a setting changes: every result records it.
qa_params_version = "1"

# A gate: every message that reached Kapto was written. An episode it
# fails isn't accepted.
[streams.complete]
max_dropped = 0
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `qa_params_version` | yes | The version of these settings, text without spaces, e.g. `3`. Recorded with every result; change it whenever a setting changes. |
| `statistics.exclude` | no | The statistics not kept, shown or compared by any detector: a list of names, where `*` stands for any part of one name between dots, e.g. `["streams.*.lost_upstream_ratio", "joints.wrist_*.jerk"]`. Every statistic is on by default, those added in later versions too. |
| `statistics.include` | no | Statistics turned back on among those `statistics.exclude` turns off, written the same way, e.g. `["streams.camera.lost_upstream_ratio"]`. |
| `streams.complete.enabled` | no | Whether the gate `streams.complete` runs: every message that reached Kapto was written. `true` by default. |
| `streams.complete.max_dropped` | no | The most messages Kapto may drop from one stream before `streams.complete` fails the episode, from 0. `0` by default. |
| `streams.present.enabled` | no | Whether the gate `streams.present` runs: every critical stream has messages in the episode. `true` by default. |
| `streams.present.critical` | no | The streams `streams.present` fails an episode without, by name, e.g. `["joints", "wrist_camera"]`. Empty by default: then every stream is, but those kept for late subscribers, which may send nothing during an episode. |
| `streams.empty.enabled` | no | Whether `streams.empty` runs: it flags each stream with no messages in the episode that `streams.present` doesn't fail it for, a stream kept for late subscribers that kept none too. Advisory. `true` by default. |
| `episode.short.enabled` | no | Whether the gate `episode.short` runs: the episode lasts at least `min_seconds`. `true` by default. |
| `episode.short.min_seconds` | no | The shortest episode accepted, in seconds, from 0 to 86400, from its first message to its end. `2` by default: shorter, it can hardly hold a task. |
| `episode.long.enabled` | no | Whether `episode.long` runs: it flags an episode longer than `max_seconds`, as one left recording does. Advisory. `true` by default. |
| `episode.long.max_seconds` | no | The longest episode not flagged, in seconds, from 1 to 86400. `600` by default. |
| `motion.jump.enabled` | no | Whether `motion.jump` runs: it flags each moment a joint moved faster than `max_speed` between two messages, as a reading that jumped does. Advisory. `true` by default. |
| `motion.jump.max_speed` | no | The fastest a joint can move, in rad/s for a turning joint or m/s for a sliding one, from 0.001 to 1000. `20` by default: faster than any arm's motors. |
| `motion.frozen.enabled` | no | Whether `motion.frozen` runs: it flags each time a joint's reading stayed exactly the same for `max_seconds` right after it moved at `moving_speed`, while another joint moved, as a reading that stopped updating does. Advisory. `true` by default. |
| `motion.frozen.max_seconds` | no | The shortest stillness flagged, in seconds, from 0.001 to 3600. `1` by default. |
| `motion.frozen.moving_speed` | no | How fast a joint must have been moving just before, in rad/s or m/s, from 0 to 1000: a joint slowing down to rest gets slower than this first. `0.05` by default. |
| `motion.chatter.enabled` | no | Whether `motion.chatter` runs: it flags a gripper (each role ending in `opening`) that closed more than `max_closings` times within `window_seconds`. Advisory. `true` by default. |
| `motion.chatter.max_closings` | no | The most closings allowed within the window, from 1 to 1000. `3` by default. |
| `motion.chatter.window_seconds` | no | The window, in seconds, from 0.001 to 3600. `2` by default. |
| `motion.idle.enabled` | no | Whether `motion.idle` runs: it flags an episode in which the robot stood still, every joint slower than `moving_speed`, for more than `max_ratio` of it, counting spans of `min_seconds` or more. Advisory. `true` by default. |
| `motion.idle.max_ratio` | no | The largest share of the episode the robot may stand still, from 0 to 1. `0.5` by default. |
| `motion.idle.min_seconds` | no | The shortest still span counted, in seconds, from 0.001 to 3600: shorter pauses are part of the task. `2` by default. |
| `motion.idle.moving_speed` | no | Slower than this, in rad/s or m/s, a joint counts as still, from 0 to 1000. `0.05` by default. |
| `anomalies.statistics.enabled` | no | Whether `anomalies.statistics` runs: it flags an episode whose statistics are far from those of the other episodes of its session (the same robot package, profile and task, on the same day). It only flags, never rejects. `true` by default. |
| `anomalies.statistics.threshold` | no | How far from the session's median a statistic must be to be flagged, in robust standard deviations (1.4826 times the median absolute deviation), from 1 to 100. `3.5` by default. |
| `anomalies.statistics.min_episodes` | no | How many other checked episodes the session needs before an episode is compared with them, from 1 to 1000. `5` by default. |
| `anomalies.statistics.max_episodes` | no | How many of the session's other episodes an episode is compared with at most, the newest, from 1 to 10000. `200` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.enabled` | no | Whether `anomalies.autoencoder` runs: it learns which statistics go together from the accepted episodes of the robot package and task, and flags an episode whose mix of statistics it can't reconstruct. It only flags, never rejects; until it has learned from `min_episodes` episodes it says how many more it needs. `true` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.model` | no | Which autoencoder: `"linear"`, principal components, which learn straight-line relations in milliseconds; or `"neural"`, a small neural network, which learns curved ones too (effort growing with the square of speed) in seconds. `"linear"` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.neurons` | no | How many neurons each of the neural autoencoder's two hidden layers has, from 1 to 256: more learn more detail and take longer. Read only for `model = "neural"`. `16` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.train_seconds` | no | How long learning a model may take, in seconds, from 0.001 to 3600; if it takes longer it stops, the previous model stays in use and each result says so. `60` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.threshold` | no | How far beyond the usual reconstruction error an episode must be to be flagged, in robust standard deviations of the errors of the episodes learned from, from 1 to 100. `3.5` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.min_episodes` | no | How many accepted episodes of the package and task are needed before a model is learned, from 3 to 10000. `20` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.max_episodes` | no | How many of them, the newest, a model learns from at most, from 3 to 10000. `200` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.variance` | no | How much of the spread of the statistics the model keeps, from 0.5 to 1: the more, the closer it follows the episodes learned from. `0.9` by default. |
| `anomalies.autoencoder.retrain_after` | no | How many new accepted episodes of the package and task make it learn again, from 1 to 10000. `10` by default. |

## `layout.toml`

How the live view and replays are arranged: columns side by side, each a
stack of panels, the timeline always under them. Below a width of 70rem
the columns stack, in order. A package without one is shown with a layout
made from what it declares: the robot on the left if a joint of it moves;
on the right each camera, a plot per group of roles (the joints' positions
first), a plot per stream of the fields no role covers (but its counters
and clocks, which only ever climb); the streams' health is beside the view
in the console. At most 24 panels: beyond, the page can't
keep its frame rate. A panel naming a stream, field or role the package
doesn't have is shown as a placeholder saying what is missing. A layout
saved as the package's default, `layouts/<package id>.toml` in the
configuration folder (`PUT /api/layout`), comes before the package's own,
in every browser, until it is removed (`DELETE /api/layout`).

```toml
[[columns]]
width = 3
panels = [
  { kind = "robot", height = 3 },
  { kind = "camera", stream = "wrist_camera" },
]

[[columns]]
width = 2
panels = [
  { kind = "plot", fields = ["arm_joints.joint_positions"], height = 2 },
  { kind = "plot", fields = ["role:gripper.opening"] },
  { kind = "health" },
]
```

Each `[[columns]]` table:

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | no | Its width relative to the other columns', a whole number from 1 to 12. 1 if not given. |
| `panels` | yes | Its panels from top to bottom, each an inline table with a `kind`. |

Each panel:

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | yes | What it shows: `robot` (the 3D view), `camera` (one camera stream), `plot` (fields over time), `health` (the streams' counts) or `events` (the timeline's marks as a list). |
| `height` | no | Its height relative to the other panels' in its column, a whole number from 1 to 12. 1 if not given. |
| `stream` | no | A `camera` panel's stream, by its ID. Only for `camera`, which needs it. |
| `fields` | no | A `plot` panel's fields, 1 to 16: each a stream's field, `stream.field` or `stream.field[3]`, or a role, `role:gripper.opening`. Only for `plot`, which needs them. |

## Identity

A version of a package is identified by its `id` and `version`, and by
its content hash, which changes whenever any of its files does, even if
the version wasn't raised. The hash is SHA-256 over one line per file,
`<SHA-256 of the file>  <path>`, with paths relative to the package
folder and separated by `/`, sorted in byte order, each line ending in a
newline. Files and folders whose names start with a dot are left out, so
a `.git` folder or an editor's leftovers don't change it. It is what
`sha256sum` gives, so it can be checked without Kapto:

```sh
cd packages/arm7
find . -type f ! -path '*/.*' | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum
```

A package holds only plain files and folders with UTF-8 names: Kapto
refuses symbolic links rather than follow them out of the package.

## Lint rules

`kapto package lint` loads a package the way Kapto does to run it and
reports every problem with its file and line where it has them, and
what to do. An error means Kapto can't use the package; a warning that
it can, with something missing. The command fails on errors only;
`--format json` gives the same report for tools.

| Code | Severity | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `package.not_found` | error | The folder has a `package.toml`. |
| `package.unknown_key` | error | `package.toml` has only keys Kapto knows. |
| `config.invalid_syntax` | error | `package.toml`, `streams.toml`, `mapping.toml` and `qa.toml` are valid TOML. |
| `config.invalid_value` | error | Every value in them has the right type and range, and every required one is there. |
| `package.missing_file` | error | The URDF, `streams.toml` and `mapping.toml` that `package.toml` names are there. |
| `package.unsafe_path` | error | The package is plain files and folders with UTF-8 names, without symbolic links. |
| `robot.urdf_invalid` | error | The URDF is valid: every link and joint well formed, every moving joint with a `<limit>`. |
| `robot.kinematic_tree_invalid` | error | The joints form one tree from a single root link. |
| `robot.joint_range_empty` | warning | Each joint that moves within limits has a lower limit below its upper one. |
| `robot.joint_limits_unknown` | warning | Each joint that moves within limits has a velocity and an effort limit. |
| `robot.mesh_unreadable` | warning | Every mesh and texture the URDF refers to is there and readable; without it, its part isn't shown. |
| `robot.mesh_unsupported_format` | warning | Every mesh is STL, OBJ, COLLADA or glTF. |
| `robot.mesh_invalid` | warning | Every mesh file is valid in its format. |
| `robot.mesh_y_up` | warning | No mesh says it was made with Y up. |
| `stream.unknown_key` | error | `streams.toml` has only keys Kapto knows. |
| `decoder.invalid_layout` | error | Every stream's decoder fields are valid. |
| `mapping.unknown_key` | error | `mapping.toml` has only keys Kapto knows. |
| `qa.unknown_key` | error | `qa.toml` has only the quality checks' settings, each in the table named after its check. |
| `layout.unknown_key` | error | The layout, if the package has one, has only columns of panels and their keys. |
| `mapping.unknown_joint` | error | Every joint `mapping.toml` maps is a moving joint of the robot. |
| `mapping.unknown_field` | error | Every field `mapping.toml` names is decoded by its stream, and is a number. |
| `mapping.unit_mismatch` | error | Every mapped field's unit fits its joint: radians for turning joints, metres for sliding ones. |
| `mapping.joint_unmapped` | warning | Every moving joint has a position mapped; without one it stays at 0 in the live view. |

A problem in `package.toml` stops the checks after it, since it names
the other files. A problem in one of those stops only the checks that
need that file; checking the mapping needs all three.
